<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD is a typical AUR VCS package that fetches an upstream GTK theme and applies additional fixes from a separate repository. The structure is standard: git sources in the `source` array with SKIP checksums (expected for git), a `prepare()` function that copies fix files and patches the upstream build scripts, and a `package()` function that runs the upstream installer with specific options inside `$pkgdir`.  

The only potentially notable point is the conditional `local_build` variable that skips fetching the fixes repo and instead copies from a path on the builder’s filesystem. This is a development convenience, not a supply-chain attack: it is gated behind an explicit environment variable (`local_build=true`) and is clearly documented in comments. No data exfiltration, no hidden downloads, no obfuscated commands, and no execution of attacker-controlled code outside the declared upstream repos. All sed operations modify only the theme’s own build scripts to correct behavior (e.g., removing a redundant `install_app` function, adjusting titlebutton imports for the “alt” variant).  

The wrapper script created in `/usr/bin/mactahoe-firefox-theme` merely invokes a shipped tweaks.sh, which is normal for Firefox theme integration. There is no evidence of malicious intent or deviation from standard packaging practices.
</details>
<evidence></evidence>
<summary>Standard AUR git package with no malicious behavior.</summary>
</security_assessment>
